newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums steady, barge demand flat.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums steady, barge demand flat.

text.p: Modest demand into Germany and France helped support NWE gas oil cargo premiums in the face of abundant supply on Tuesday but some players remained out of the market due to recent screen volatility, traders said.
Benchmark Jan IPE futures slipped 50 cents to $222 a tonne in line with a weak opening on NYMEX, helping retrace gains made in the last two sessions.

Cargoes of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil traded into Germany at Jan IPE +$6 and +$7, although some traders said later the differential to low sulphur diesel was narrowing to around $5 on good supply.
Others said the market was well established with sellers hard to find and a differential at around $11.
A low sulphur diesel was done into Le Havre at $16.75 for delivery before December 25, up to $1.50 firmer.
Russians are long with premiums at around Jan IPE 0.75/1.75.
But trade is slowing as players wind up business for Christmas and New Year. "The market will spring back to life from January 6 when people get back," a trader said.
Barges were weak and inactive with premiums at Jan IPE -$2/-0.50. Low sulphur was around Jan IPE +$10/11.
